rounds.diagnosis: The pour stage constrains teapot.+front parallel to mug.+up, which points the spout upward instead of down into the mug. With spout_tip pinned 8-10 cm over the opening this rolls the body below the mug rim (handle at -12.4 cm), and the renderer finds no collision-free pose anywhere in the subgoal region (teapot vs mug and table), with the path bounds equally unusable. Flipping the constrained direction to teapot.-front parallel mug.up_axis on both the subgoal and path rotation rows gives the intended spout-down pour pose with the body above the mug, matching the stage's own goal text.

rounds.diagnosis: Both editable stages constrain what matters: the carry holds the pot upright with tight roll/pitch while leaving translation free for collision avoidance, and ends with the spout tip centered and well above the mug rim; the pour holds the spout tip over the opening throughout a roll band that spans only the intended forward tilt, with pitch tight so the stream stays on the mug. Nominal-pose collisions reported are resolvable inside the regions and are the planner's responsibility.
